body:
Closing without merge after mathematical reproduction and an in-depth priority audit. The scoped coarse-point theorem and explicit computations passed independent mathematical reviews; the rejection is a priority issue.

The claimed universal bound is a short consequence of earlier general descent theory. For the coarse PGL2-homogeneous fiber F, form the residual gerbe [F/PGL2] and its associated projective-line family. Its compression is a genus-zero curve Y. A point of the free open of Y gives both a PGL2-torsor and a rational point of its associated conic, so that torsor is split and yields an ordinary coarse Hurwitz point on the fixed split line. Every nonempty open of a conic over an infinite characteristic-zero field has a point of degree at most two.

Moreover, Bresciani’s general gerbe result forces Y to split whenever the geometric stabilizer is noncyclic, including V4. See [arXiv:2211.03438v1 (2022), Proposition 2, pp.3–4, and Lemma 11, pp.7–8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.03438v1), published as [J. Algebra 647 (2024), 72–98](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2024.02.021), and the general-structure/compression framework in [arXiv:2303.01409v2 (2023), Theorem 2 and Lemma 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.01409v2). Necessity of the universal constant two was already recorded in [Cadoret, author manuscript, Remark 3.14, p.15](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~anna.cadoret/GPGL2.pdf) ([2008 publication](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11856-008-0019-0)).

This is an explicit implication from prior theory, not a claim that those sources state the identical Hurwitz theorem verbatim. It concerns coarse points; it does not infer descent of an actual marked cover or replace the cover-point stabilizer with the larger branch-divisor stabilizer. The explicit arithmetic example and elliptic proof remain valid contributions to the verification record, but reframing them as exposition would not repair the claim to newly resolve the original open bound. No preprint deposit or publication-tracker row is being created for this PR.
